label: Person
name: Lu Ji
summary:
Lu Ji, courtesy name Shiheng, was a Chinese essayist, military general, politician, and writer who lived during the late Three Kingdoms period and Jin dynasty of China. Born into the prominent family of Lu Kang, a general of the state of Eastern Wu, he was the grandson of Lu Xun, a renowned general and statesman.

Lu Ji rose to prominence in the late 3rd century CE, serving as a military general under the Jin dynasty and later becoming an influential figure in Chinese politics. He is best known for his essays, which showcased his mastery of classical Chinese literature and philosophical thought.

Throughout his life, Lu Ji navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various kingdoms and dynasties of ancient China. His experiences during this period shaped his writings, which often explored themes of loyalty, duty, and the human condition.

Lu Ji's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his essays have had a lasting impact on Chinese literature and continue to be studied by scholars today.

"The Art of Rhetoric," "The Art of War," and “A Discourse on Salt and Pepper” are some of his notable works.

Lu Ji died in 303 CE, at the age of unknown, leaving behind a body of work that continues to be celebrated for its literary merit and historical significance.
